title: Non-blocking follow-ups from backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups-followups-followups's PR #355 review
description: PR #355 (backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups-followups-followups) shared one find_swing_points pass across current_divergence's 3 indicators and was accepted after independent re-verification (own hand-computed cross-indicator-tie-break scenario, 200-trial differential fuzz test, mutation test re-run, speedup reproduction, verify-elder-signal check finding no methodology drift). This tracks the review's non-blocking findings so they aren't lost once the PR merges.

checklist.step: PR #355 review (backgrounded code-review skill pass, high effort): `current_divergence` now calls `find_swing_points(price, window=window)` unconditionally at the top of the function, before checking whether any of macd_histogram/stochastic/rsi was actually supplied -- a genuine behavior change from pre-fix `main`, verified directly: `current_divergence(price, window=0)` with all three indicators left at their `None` default returns `None` on `main` (no indicator branch ever executes, so `find_swing_points` is never called) but raises `ValueError('window must be >= 1 (got 0)')` post-fix. Separately confirmed that even with a valid window, calling `current_divergence` with zero indicators now performs one wasted full-history `find_swing_points` scan that pre-fix never did (verified via a wraps-spy: 1 call vs 0). Not reachable today -- `app.signals.engine`'s only call site always supplies all three indicators with the default (valid) window, and no API-level parameter exposes a caller-controlled `window` for divergence -- but a real narrowing of the public function's documented contract ('any subset ... a None series is simply skipped'). Fix: guard the eager `find_swing_points` call behind `if macd_histogram is not None or stochastic is not None or rsi is not None:` (or compute the swing lists lazily on first actual need), with a regression test covering the zero-indicators-plus-invalid-window case.

PR #355 review (same code-review pass): `_latest_divergence_from_swings` duplicates `latest_divergence`'s own tie-break logic (bullish-then-bearish candidate list via `divergences_from_swings`, `max(..., key=lambda d: d.second.date)`) instead of `latest_divergence` delegating to the new shared-swings helper -- a maintenance hazard: a future change to the tie-break rule applied to only one of the two now-duplicated copies would silently desync `latest_divergence` and `current_divergence`'s per-indicator result, and the PR's own cross-check tests (`test_current_divergence_matches_per_indicator_latest_divergence`) wouldn't catch the drift since they only run today's already-matching logic. Worth refactoring: have `latest_divergence` itself call `swing_lows(price, window=window)`/`swing_highs(price, window=window)` once and delegate into `_latest_divergence_from_swings`, removing the duplicated tie-break code entirely.

PR #355 review (same code-review pass, cosmetic): the bearish-only `price`/`histogram` fixture in `tests/unit/signals/test_divergence.py` is copy-pasted verbatim between `test_current_divergence_picks_up_a_bearish_divergence_via_shared_highs` and `test_current_divergence_is_not_stale_across_consecutive_calls_with_different_price`, instead of being hoisted to a module-level `_FIXTURE_B_PRICE`/`_FIXTURE_B_MACD_HISTOGRAM` pair matching the file's existing `_FIXTURE_A_*` convention.

PR #355 review finding: the PR description and this task's own filing task's `decisions` entry both claim '35 pre-existing hand-computed-value tests... pass unchanged; added 7 new tests'. Independently counted: the pre-existing file had 29 tests (not 35), and the PR adds 6 new tests (the `TestCurrentDivergenceSharedSwingPass` class has 6 methods, not 7) -- 29 + 6 = 35 total, so the final total happens to be correct, but both individual figures are off by one. Documentation-accuracy nit -- worth a corrective `decisions` entry (append-only, per CLAUDE.md) on `backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups-followups-followups.json` next time it's touched.

PR #355 review finding: `backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups-followups-followups.json`'s own `decisions` entry claims `latest_divergence` is 'still used directly by GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis's whole-history divergence display'. Verified this is inaccurate: that endpoint's divergence data flows through `app.signals.engine.analyse`'s call to `current_divergence` (the only caller of `current_divergence` in `app/`), and post-PR-#355 `current_divergence` no longer calls `latest_divergence` at all internally (it calls `_latest_divergence_from_swings` instead). `latest_divergence` now has zero callers outside its own module and the test suite -- it remains a correct, independently-tested public function, just not wired into any production code path today. Worth a corrective `decisions` entry (append-only) next time that task file is touched.

PR #355 review finding: the checklist-item-4 wording-tweak `decisions` entry on `backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups-followups-followups.json` (and its mirrored entry on `backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups-followups.json`) cites CLAUDE.md's narrow 'amending an existing decisions entry's text in place' carve-out as authority for editing the OTHER task's checklist-item `step` text -- but that carve-out, by its own text, is scoped specifically to correcting a stale claim inside an already-done task's `decisions` entry, not to checklist `step` text; CLAUDE.md never states this carve-out extends to checklist items. The actual edit holds up on its own terms regardless (it was independently and explicitly authorized by the filing task's own checklist item 2's 'worth a human sanity-check / wording tweak next time that task file is touched' instruction, and was executed conservatively as a non-destructive bracketed append with a fresh decisions entry) -- but the specific authority cited is a category mismatch. Worth either (a) a fresh, narrow decisions-entry correction noting the more precise authorizing source, or (b) raising to a human whether CLAUDE.md's in-place-edit carve-out should be explicitly extended to cover checklist-item text too, given this is likely to recur.

decisions.decision: Guarded `current_divergence`'s eager `find_swing_points(price, window=window)` call behind `if macd_histogram is not None or stochastic is not None or rsi is not None:` (chose the guard form the checklist item itself suggested over lazily computing swing lists on first actual need per-indicator, since a per-indicator lazy computation would reintroduce a subtler version of the exact redundancy this whole PR chain exists to remove -- e.g. macd_histogram and stochastic each independently triggering the same lazy computation on first use -- whereas the simple upfront boolean guard preserves the single-shared-computation property for every actually-reachable (>=1 indicator) call, at the cost of one trivial boolean check for the unreachable-today zero-indicator case).
decisions.rationale: Verified both halves of the bug directly: `current_divergence(_FIXTURE_A_PRICE, window=0)` now returns `None` instead of raising (added as `test_current_divergence_with_no_indicators_and_invalid_window_returns_none`), and a `wraps`-spy on `find_swing_points` confirms zero calls (not one) for a zero-indicators call with a valid window (added as `test_current_divergence_with_no_indicators_never_calls_find_swing_points`). Ran the full `tests/unit/signals/test_divergence.py` suite (39 tests, up from 37) plus the full backend suite/coverage/static-analysis afterward -- all pass, 100% coverage maintained. Not reachable from any production call site today (confirmed via grep: `app.signals.engine`'s only call site always supplies all three indicators with the default valid window), matching this finding's own framing, so this is a contract-correctness fix, not a behavior change any current caller can observe.

decisions.decision: Refactored `latest_divergence` to delegate to `_latest_divergence_from_swings` (computing `swing_lows(price, window=window)`/`swing_highs(price, window=window)` once, then calling the shared helper) instead of independently building its own bullish-then-bearish candidate list via two `find_divergences` calls and its own `max(..., key=lambda d: d.second.date)`. `_latest_divergence_from_swings` (used by both `latest_divergence` and `current_divergence` now) is the single remaining copy of the tie-break logic; its docstring was updated to describe itself as the shared source of truth rather than as a helper `latest_divergence` merely 'mirrors'. Left `_pick_most_recent`/`_INDICATOR_PRIORITY` (the cross-INDICATOR tie-break, a distinct concern) untouched, and did not reorder the two functions' definitions in the file (Python resolves the `latest_divergence` -> `_latest_divergence_from_swings` name reference at call time, not definition time, so the existing top-to-bottom reading order -- `latest_divergence` before the newer `_latest_divergence_from_swings` it now calls -- was kept rather than moved, to minimize the diff).
decisions.rationale: Mutation-tested the dedup directly per this session's own verification standard: confirmed only ONE occurrence of `key=lambda d: d.second.date` remains in the module (in `_latest_divergence_from_swings` itself -- grepped to confirm `latest_divergence` no longer has its own copy), then temporarily changed that single `max(...)` to `min(...)` (reintroducing a divergent tie-break) and re-ran `tests/unit/signals/test_divergence.py`: exactly 2 tests failed -- both newly added by this task (`test_latest_divergence_prefers_the_more_recent_of_bullish_and_bearish` and `test_current_divergence_agrees_with_latest_divergence_on_a_two_candidate_fixture`), both asserting `result.kind == 'bearish'` and instead getting `'bullish'` -- then reverted the mutation and confirmed the file was byte-identical to pre-mutation and the full suite passed again (39/39). This also surfaced a genuine pre-existing coverage gap this task closes: every other fixture in the file qualifies on only ONE kind (bullish or bearish) at a time, so `_latest_divergence_from_swings`'s own `max`-by-date selection across a genuine 2-candidate (bullish AND bearish) list was never actually exercised before -- a new `_FIXTURE_C_PRICE`/`_FIXTURE_C_MACD_HISTOGRAM` pair (a single series qualifying on both kinds, with the bearish pair's `second.date` chronologically after the bullish pair's) was added specifically to give the mutation something to be caught by, and is kept as a permanent regression test beyond just this mutation-testing exercise, since it hand-verified the real selection behavior (`latest_divergence`/`current_divergence` correctly picking the more recent bearish result over the older bullish one) that had never been directly tested. Additionally ran a 300-trial randomized differential fuzz test (independent of and in addition to the hand-computed suite) comparing this refactor's `current_divergence`/`latest_divergence` against the pre-refactor implementation loaded fresh from `git show origin/main:backend/app/signals/divergence.py` -- varying series length, random-walk price, which of macd_histogram/stochastic/rsi are populated (each independently ~85% likely), and `window` (2-5): zero `dataclasses.asdict` mismatches across all 300 `current_divergence` trials and every per-indicator `latest_divergence` cross-check within them.

decisions.decision: Hoisted the bearish-only `price`/`histogram` fixture duplicated between `test_current_divergence_picks_up_a_bearish_divergence_via_shared_highs` and `test_current_divergence_is_not_stale_across_consecutive_calls_with_different_price` to module-level `_FIXTURE_B_PRICE`/`_FIXTURE_B_MACD_HISTOGRAM` constants, matching the file's existing `_FIXTURE_A_*` naming convention, and updated both tests to reference them. Deliberately left the pre-existing, unrelated `test_bearish_divergence_is_the_mirror_case` test (which happens to construct numerically-identical `price`/`histogram` values inline, predating this PR chain) untouched -- the checklist item's own wording scopes this specifically to 'between two new tests' (the two named above), and folding in a third, older, not-reviewer-flagged test would be scope creep beyond what this finding asked for.
decisions.rationale: Straightforward mechanical deduplication with no behavior change -- verified by re-running `tests/unit/signals/test_divergence.py` (still 39 passing, same assertions, same fixture values) after the edit.

Items 4-6's decisions corrections diffed against each ancestor task's actual pre-PR revision (resolved via `git log --follow`, not blindly against current main, per the task's own instruction): docs/tasks/done/backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups-followups-followups.json diffed against e423951 (its last modification before this PR) shows a pure append of 3 new decisions entries with zero changes to any existing entry's text, checklist, or other fields. docs/tasks/done/backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups-followups.json diffed against the same commit e423951 shows a pure append of 1 new decisions entry, likewise with no edits to existing text. No UI-facing surface (no frontend/API-consumer change), so the browser walkthrough (step 9) and persisted e2e suite (step 9a) are both explicitly not applicable and were skipped. This is a pre-existing condition this PR's refactor simply extends one level further (current_divergence never called latest_divergence even pre-#357, and latest_divergence itself already had zero production callers per this task's own item-5 finding), not a new regression, but worth a documentation pass on find_divergences's own docstring or a task decisions entry noting it's now test-only/reference surface. A backgrounded code-review skill pass (high effort) found: (1) the new `_FIXTURE_B_*` module-level comment claims 'every other current_divergence test in this file exercises the bullish/lows side only', but this PR's own new `test_current_divergence_agrees_with_latest_divergence_on_a_two_candidate_fixture` also gets a bearish `current_divergence` result (via FIXTURE_C's multi-candidate tie-break) -- a documentation-accuracy nit introduced by this very diff, cosmetic. Both non-blocking; filed as checklist items on the new follow-up task.
